Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Should I repot it? Or I could just add soil on top of it?

I have it for almost 2yrs now. I haven’t done anything to it. Any advice?

I can use regular potting soil for it? Or bonsai soil would be the best option? I want to repot it for a long time now but most of the blogs i’ve read is too much for me. Like the layers of the soil needed, the specific pot to be used, etc.

Im treating it as a normal houseplant.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause:** Nothing alarming. The leaves look glossy and healthy, and the exposed trunk base and surface roots are normal for this style. The likely issue is that the plant has been in the same compacted nursery mix for two years. Two to three years is the usual [repotting window](https://www.bonsaiempire.com/tree-species/ficus), so it's due.

**Do this first:** Push a finger about an inch into the soil. If it's dry, water until it runs out the drainage holes. If it's damp, wait. Don't add soil on top, since that won't refresh the root zone.

**Then:**
- Check that the pot has drainage holes. Many store-bought ficus come in [dense potting soil](https://www.bonsaioutlet.com/ginseng-grafted-ficus-care/), so this matters.
- In spring, repot into a fast-draining bonsai mix in a pot only slightly larger. Trim no more than about a third of the roots.
- Feed lightly during spring and summer, and only when the soil is moist.
- Keep it in bright, indirect light away from drafts.

**If that's not it:**
- **Overwatering or root rot:** Soil stays wet, the base feels soft or looks dark, or the stems turn [mushy](https://cafeplanta.com/a/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-watering-ficus-microcarpa). Lift it out and cut away brown, mushy roots.
- **Too little light:** Leaves drop, new leaves stay small, and growth leans toward the window. Move it closer to a bright window.
